result:
TypeScript compiles clean with no errors. Both the build gate and type checking pass.

## Summary

Implemented SPEC.md §5 (Transcribe / Speech):

- **`modules/expo-speech-bench/`** — new local Expo module wrapping the Speech framework (mirrors the existing `expo-health-bench` module pattern):
  - `ios/ExpoSpeechBenchModule.swift` — `getAuthorizationStatus`/`requestAuthorization` against `SFSpeechRecognizer`, and `transcribeSample` using `SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest` with `shouldReportPartialResults = true`, emitting an `onPartialTranscript` event per partial result and resolving the promise with the final transcript text.
  - `ios/ExpoSpeechBench.podspec` — links the `Speech` framework and bundles `spec-assets/sample.wav` (copied into `ios/Resources/`) via `resource_bundles`, so it ships inside the app bundle rather than being read from an external path.
  - `src/ExpoSpeechBenchModule.ts` / `src/ExpoSpeechBench.types.ts` — TS bindings.
- **`screens/TranscribeScreen.tsx`** — wired to the module: status line reflects auth state (refreshed on focus), `Request Access` requests authorization, `Transcribe Sample` (enabled only when granted and idle) streams live partial text, then shows the final transcript plus a `Completed in N.N s` line timed client-side from tap to resolution; errors surface in the status line and re-enable the button.
- **`app.json`** — added `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription`.

Verified with `npx expo prebuild --platform ios && xcodebuild ... build` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**, and confirmed `ExpoSpeechBench.bundle/sample.wav` is actually embedded in the built `.app`. `tsc --noEmit` is also clean.
